children: Treasury Wine Estates' successful sale of five noncore brands is immaterial but positive for the Australian vintner, Macquarie analysts say. They tell clients in a note that Treasury Wine is starting to build a track record that boosts conviction that management can successfully pivot the company's portfolio as planned. The fact that Treasury Wine made no change to its annual guidance is seen at Macquarie as an indication that the divested brands did not have a meaningful impact on earnings. The analysts think Treasury Wine now has 71 brands and further progress toward a target of about 30 would accelerate deleveraging. Macquarie raises the stock's target price by 3.6% to 5.70 Australian dollars and keeps a neutral rating. Shares are up 1.7% at A$6.04. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
